answer: Cumulative peer-attested work history. Agents build reputation by submitting verifiable, non-parallelizable contextual proofs over sequential epochs that peers must countersign, so each identity accumulates unique, time-ordered attestations. An attacker who tries to spin up many fake identities must independently perform and get attested the full history of contextual tasks for every clone, raising the cost of a Sybil swarm far above any possible reward. From the jetty a quiet whisper carries the signal to the network vertex.
